description: Page content types for the CMS framework: PageContent, the page tree attributes and IPageService. Reference it from the project holding your content types; Ark.Framework.Pages does the rest.
releaseNotes:
v9.2.0: Editor UI polish, page drag and drop into reference fields, change or cancel publish schedules

**Changed for code that implements `IContentEditingService`**
- The interface has a new member, `CancelPublishSchedule(id, language, versionNumber)`. A class of a site's own that implements the interface (a decorator, say) must add it; code that only calls the service needs no change.

**New**
- Publish schedules can be changed and cancelled. `DELETE /api/content/{id}/publish-schedule?language=&versionNumber=` (`CancelPublishSchedule` in `@arkframework/cms/client`):
  - For a version scheduled to go live, it cancels the publish: the version is a draft again, and the version live now stays live if it was only to stop when the scheduled one took over.
  - For the live version, it cancels its scheduled end: it stays live.
  - An end that is a scheduled version's start is refused with 409 (cancel that publish instead), as is a version with nothing scheduled.
  - Changing a time is still `POST /{id}/publish` (a version that hasn't gone live is rescheduled in place) or `POST /{id}/unpublish` with a new `stopPublish`.
- CMS edit view: a three-dot menu on the publish button. It lists what is scheduled in the language - change or cancel a scheduled publish of a version, change or cancel the scheduled unpublish - and Move to rubbish bin, which moved there from the form footer. Without a publish button the menu is a button of its own.
- CMS: pages dragged from the page tree can be dropped on ContentReference and ContentReferenceList (content area) properties, as on LinkUrl ones before. A content area inserts the page where it is dropped. A page of a type the property doesn't allow can't be dropped, and the field says so.
- CMS: ContentReference and LinkUrl fields start with an icon - a document for a content reference, a link for a link - so the two can be told apart.

**Changed in the CMS UI**
- Content areas (ContentReferenceList): one bordered area like an input, with a full-width Add button inside it and "Drag and drop content here, or create new" when empty.
- Reference rows show the content type's display name in the metadata header's type, and are as tall as a text input (growing with the font instead of clipping).
- A reference's Edit link opens in the same tab. It is a real link, so open in new tab still works; the edit view asks before leaving unsaved changes.
- Change on ContentReference and LinkUrl fields shows on hover or keyboard focus; Clear stays visible.
- Text areas and editable MarkdownDocument fields have a resize handle and grow with their text where the browser supports `field-sizing: content`. The Markdown editor has a resize handle too.
- Settings > Languages: the master language dropdown has the same input style as the other fields.
- The create page's Content type and Master language dropdowns (and the content type picker in the reference dialog) are as tall as the other inputs.
- The publish button's more menu shows vertical dots.

**Fixed**
- Secondary text in the CMS UI - the content type above a referenced item, metadata labels, notes, list details - showed in the primary text colour since the move to MUI 9, which ignores Typography's `color="text.secondary"`. It is the secondary colour again.

No migrations.
